goal.source_text: Make the fins at least 25% lighter without adding drag. Keep the stability margin at least 1.5 calibers and the flutter margin at least 1.5. You can change anything except the fin count.

constraints.label: 25% lighter than current total fin mass

assumptions: Darwin may change root_chord, taper_ratio, semi_span, sweep_deg, thickness, edge_profile; it holds fin_count fixed.
25% lighter is applied to total fin mass: 60.264 g x 0.75 = 45.198 g for all fins.
No added drag means drag_n must not exceed its current 9.7832 N.
Keeping the current fin count of 3.

payload.explanation: Reducing semi-span decreased stability margin by 25.8% (to 1.13), violating the 1.5 limit, so design was rejected. Drag and mass dropped 8.33% as predicted, but flutter margin unexpectedly rose 11.7% because shorter span increased stiffness. Predictions for mass/drag were accurate; stability was slightly worse than predicted, flutter direction wrong.
payload.lesson: Semi-span cuts stability more than expected while improving flutter; thickness drives flutter more.

Stability margin stayed ~+1.89%. Predictions for mass and stability were accurate, but flutter and drag were off.
payload.lesson: Reducing thickness from 3 mm to 2.5 mm severely degrades flutter margin; maintain thickness unless flutter is reassessed.

payload.lesson: Reducing root chord lowers fin mass but barely affects drag; flutter margin may improve.

payload.lesson: Stability margin is the binding constraint; reducing fin area must preserve margin ≥1.5.

payload.lesson: Increasing sweep does not always improve stability; check CP shift direction.
